content: 1. Cobicistat and Nortriptyline: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of nortriptyline by mechanisms involving hepatic or intestinal enzyme interactions. Careful dose titration of nortriptyline is required to achieve the desired therapeutic effect. Start with the lowest feasible dose and monitor the response closely during coadministration with cobicistat. 2. Darunavir and Olaparib: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of olaparib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose to 200 mg (capsule) or 150 mg (tablet) twice daily. For strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the dose further to 150 mg (capsule) or 100 mg (tablet) twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. 3. Cobicistat and Oliceridine: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. 4. Darunavir and Oliceridine: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Similar to cobicistat, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust doses as needed. If the inhibitor is discontinued, increase the oliceridine dosage to maintain therapeutic effects. 5. Darunavir and Omaveloxolone: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day. Monitor closely for adverse effects and discontinue if necessary. 6. Cobicistat and Omaveloxolone: Cobicistat also increases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone via CYP3A4 inhibition. Follow the same precautions as with darunavir. 7. Cobicistat and Ombitasvir/Paritaprevir/Ritonavir: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of this combination by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 8. Darunavir and Ombitasvir/Paritaprevir/Ritonavir: Darunavir also increases the levels or effects of this combination via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration. 9. Cobicistat and Omeprazole: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Darunavir and Ondansetron: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment is recommended. 11. Cobicistat and Ondansetron: Cobicistat also increases the levels or effects of ondansetron via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Orlistat and Darunavir: Orlistat decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and if an increased viral load is confirmed, discontinue orlistat. 13. Darunavir and Osilodrostat: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of osilodrostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the osilodrostat dose by half when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 14. Cobicistat and Osilodrostat: Cobicistat also increases the levels or effects of osilodrostat via CYP3A4 inhibition. Follow the same precautions as with darunavir. 15. Cobicistat and Osimertinib: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of osimertinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 16. Darunavir and Osimertinib: Darunavir also increases the levels or effects of osimertinib via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration. If no alternative exists, monitor the patient closely for adverse effects. 17. Darunavir and Ospemifene: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ospemifene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Cobicistat and Ospemifene: Cobicistat also increases the levels or effects of ospemifene via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Oxcarbazepine and Darunavir: Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 20. Oxcarbazepine and Cobicistat: Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Darunavir and Oxybutynin: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of oxybutynin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 22. Cobicistat and Oxycodone: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of oxycodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. A dose reduction of oxycodone may be warranted. 23. Darunavir and Oxycodone: Darunavir also increases the levels or effects of oxycodone via CYP3A4 inhibition. Follow the same precautions as with cobicistat. 24. Cobicistat and Ozanimod: Cobicistat increases the toxicity of ozanimod by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 25. Cobicistat and Paclitaxel: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 26. Darunavir and Paclitaxel: Darunavir also increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely. 27. Cobicistat and Pacritinib: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pacritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 28. Darunavir and Pacritinib: Darunavir also increases the levels or effects of pacritinib via CYP3A4 inhibition. Coadministration is contraindicated. 29. Cobicistat and Palbociclib: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 30. Darunavir and Palbociclib: Darunavir also increases the levels or effects of palbociclib via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. 31. Darunavir and Palovarotene: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of palovarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 32. Cobicistat and Palovarotene: Cobicistat also increases the levels or effects of palovarotene via CYP3A4 inhibition. Follow the same precautions as with darunavir.
